classification.difficultyReason: Infer the square's side from a semicircle's radius, then subtract two semicircular areas from the square.

content.prompt: Two semicircles, each of radius $5\text{ cm}$, are cut from a square, as shown below.

spec.description: An unshaded square with inward-facing semicircles whose diameters are its left and right sides. The arcs touch at the square's centre. Both diameter midpoints are marked. Ordinary source blue outlines and red centre markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: Each semicircle has radius 5 cm. The upper half of the left side and lower half of the right side are each labelled 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source geometry, centre markers and the two supplied radius labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the side length of the square?

answer.worked:
The square's side is the diameter of either semicircle.

$$\begin{align*}s&=2\times5\\s&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the approximate value of the remaining area? Use $\pi\approx3.14$.

answer.short:
$21.5\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the two semicircles, which together have the area of one circle, from the square.
answer.worked:
The two semicircles together have the area of one circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{remaining}}&=10^2-2\left(\frac12\pi\times5^2\right)\\A_{\text{remaining}}&=100-25\pi\\A_{\text{remaining}}&\approx100-25\times3.14\\A_{\text{remaining}}&\approx21.5\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
